items.difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-shriek, for composable morphisms f : X -> Y and g : Y -> Z of FTS_S, the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism (g o f)^! -> f^! o g^! (statement lines 4160-4165). The construction chooses a compactification i : Y -> Ybar of Y over Z and then X -> Xbar of X over Ybar, using More on Flatness, Theorem labelled flat-theorem-nagata and Lemma labelled flat-lemma-compactifyable twice; with a-bar and b-bar the right adjoints of Lemma labelled lemma-twisted-inverse-image for Xbar -> Ybar and Ybar -> Z, the composite a-bar o b-bar is the right adjoint for Xbar -> Z, so g^! = i^* o b-bar and (g o f)^! = (X -> Xbar)^* o a-bar o b-bar (proof lines 4167-4184). Letting U be the inverse image of Y in Xbar and a-bar' the right adjoint for U -> Y, one has f^! = j^* o a-bar', and the base change map gamma : (j')^* o a-bar -> a-bar' o i^* from equation labelled equation-sheafy defines the required arrow, which is an isomorphism on D_QCoh^+ by Lemma labelled lemma-proper-noetherian (proof lines 4186-4200). The rest of the proof shows independence of the choices: given two diagrams, More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-compactifications-cofiltered provides a compactification of Y dominating both, and More on Flatness, Lemma labelled flat-lemma-right-multiplicative-system with Categories, Lemmas labelled categories-lemma-morphisms-right-localization and categories-lemma-equality-morphisms-right-localization provides a compactification of X dominating both compatibly, reducing the comparison to one commutative diagram of compactifications (proof lines 4202-4266). The final step isolates the five base change maps gamma_A to gamma_E attached to the five cartesian squares, writes the required commutativity as gamma_B o gamma_E = (gamma_A o gamma_D) o gamma_C, uses Lemmas labelled lemma-compose-base-change-maps and lemma-compose-base-change-maps-horizontal to rewrite gamma_E = gamma_A o gamma_F and to move gamma_A past gamma_B, and observes that both sides are the base change map for the single square U_1 -> Xbar_1 -> Ybar_2, noting the last equality uses that the squares A and B meet in one point as in Remark labelled remark-going-around (proof lines 4268-4367). Managing the two compactification choices and the algebra of five base change maps is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
